subject: Re: Ramp gate temporary slice request and autoscale exception
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-06T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Ramp window ask — BrightHealth pilot (short reserve + autoscale exception)

Jonas,

Heads up — BrightHealth (Nolan) needs a short, controlled capacity window for a live proof-of-concept in early December. They're sensitive to latency and procurement has asked for a temporary reserved carve (not full Dedicated contract) to guarantee SLA during integration. High level ask: reserve a small slice equivalent to 4 A100-class GPUs for a 72-hour ramp window and allow an autoscale policy exception (higher queue depth and short burst) for the first 48 hours.

Why: it's a sales-critical PoC tied to DH-4729; if we miss the latency target they will push the procurement pause.

Can you confirm feasibility and what ops needs to approve? Attached a quick ramp_window_plan and the pilot Qs the customer shared.

Thanks —
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: ramp_window_plan_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
[Attachment: pilot_qs.pdf (pdf)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-06T12:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Ramp window ask — BrightHealth pilot (short reserve + autoscale exception)

Kimberly —

Thanks for the context. A few clarifying questions before I route to infra approvals:
- Exact start/end timestamps (UTC) for the 72-hour window?
- Expected concurrent requests / QPS and 95th pct token rate during the demo?
- Can this demo tolerate a brief failover to a quantized model variant if we hit resource contention?
- Is the customer open to a burst lane (short-lived preemptible capacity) + prefix caching instead of a reserved slice? That reduces cost and still maintains latency for most flows.

Operational constraints: a true dedicated carve requires a written cost cap and rollback plan. For an autoscale exception we need an ops runbook and a monitoring threshold to auto-evict if production SLAs for other customers are breached. I can run a quick feasibility pass if you can confirm the numbers.

Happy to jump on a 15-minute sync this afternoon to go through details.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Infra & Serving
Redwood Inference

Folks —

Answers inline:
- Target window: 2026-12-06T18:00:00Z to 2026-12-09T18:00:00Z (72 hours).
- Expected peak: ~220 concurrent sessions, average prompt+response token budget ~180 tokens, 95th pct throughput ~350 qps (short bursts).
- Business constraint: customer procurement requires a reservation confirmation by 2026-11-20 or they will delay signature. BrightHealth is a strategic target for our healthcare vertical — Marissa has been driving this.
- Failover: acceptable but we must not degrade P95 latency above 350ms for the demo path. Quantized variant fallback is acceptable as a last resort but not preferred.

Concrete ask: carve a temporary slice equivalent to 4 A100 GPUs (or equivalent vCPU-backed fast instances), and grant an autoscale policy exception to raise max queue depth and burst headroom for 48 hours of the 72-hour window. We'll own the smoke tests and provide a verified traffic script. Attached latency targets.

Laura Bennett
Product Manager, Dedicated
Redwood Inference

Thanks team —

Conditional approval from my side to proceed with a temporary reservation and the autoscale exception, provided the following are met before we carve resources:
1) A firm cost cap for the window (ops/finance to confirm estimate and sign-off).
2) A rollback and automated eviction policy that will drop the slice if cross-customer SLAs are at risk.
3) A short smoke test runbook (ops-owned) to be executed 24 hours before the start.
4) A one-click revert in Console if we need to immediately free capacity.

Kimberly/Marissa — please confirm customer acceptance of our rollback clause (they must accept potential temporary performance fallback in writing).

Jonas — please coordinate cost estimate and runbook; loop in Finance if the estimated spend exceeds $X,000 for the window.

— Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Field Ops & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Ramp window ask — BrightHealth pilot (short reserve + autoscale exception)

All — quick ops update and next steps:

- Feasibility: confirmed. We can create a temporary slice in our pilot pool and map it to a reserved capacity tag for 2026-12-06T18:00:00Z through 2026-12-09T18:00:00Z.
- Autoscale exception: approved for the 48-hour high-burst portion (2026-12-06T18:00:00Z to 2026-12-08T18:00:00Z) with the following guardrails: automated eviction threshold at 15% global capacity pressure, P95 latency alert at 400ms triggers immediate rollback, and a max spend cap set in the reservation.
- Cost: preliminary estimate attached (cost_estimate.csv). Ops will finalize once we pick exact instance types; if estimate > $45,000 we need Finance sign-off (looping Neha).
- Runbook & smoke test: attached runbook_rampgate.md. Ops will run smoke tests 24 hours prior and validate the traffic script Laura provided.
- Customer communication: Kimberly/Marissa please get written acceptance of the rollback clause from Nolan by 2026-11-18 to meet procurement deadline.

I'll open INF-8942 for the carve and link the HubSpot deal DH-4729. If everyone agrees I will schedule the slice creation on Monday and start reservation choreography.

Attachments: runbook_rampgate.md (text), cost_estimate.csv (csv)

Thanks —
Jonas
